title: Portfolio Analytics
description: Run pyvar's 50 portfolio-analytics functions on the live pyvar.com API: Markowitz, Black-Litterman and risk-parity optimisation, Sharpe/Sortino/drawdown, Brinson attribution, Fama-French factor models, PCA and regime detection, ESG tilts. Use when the user wants a portfolio optimised, attributed or measured with real numbers, not just the method explained. Needs a free pyvar API key; the skill explains how to get one.
tagline: Portfolio calculations: optimisation, risk-adjusted performance, attribution, factor models, active-risk analytics, ESG and drawdown. Pick the function in **Functions** below; the **Worked examples** show the request shape.

examples.title: Minimum-variance and risk-parity weights on one covariance matrix
examples.intro: A three-asset daily covariance matrix (the optimisers expect daily, not annual, covariance). Both calls return weights that sum to 1.

examples.title: Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown over two years
examples.intro: Daily returns in, annualised Sharpe and the worst peak-to-trough fall out.

notes.black_litterman_model: verified exact match to He & Litterman (1999) conventions: Omega=diag(P*tau*Sigma*P'), lambda=delta=2.5, tau=0.05 are their specific default choices. Takes p_matrix/q_views directly (no natural-language view parsing) and returns posterior_returns, implied_returns and weights — NOT the weights/return/volatility/sharpe shape used by the mean-variance-family functions below.
notes.currency_attribution: naive geometric local/FX split via base=(1+local)(1+fx)-1, with currency as the residual. This is NOT Karnosky-Singer (Karnosky & Singer 1994): that method needs local returns net of the local risk-free rate and moves the rate differential onto the currency leg via covered interest parity; this function takes no interest rates at all. A prior docstring claimed "Karnosky-Singer style" — corrected in the citation cleanup pass (engine/portfolio_attribution.py). See Bacon (2008), "Practical Portfolio Performance Measurement and Attribution", 2nd ed., Ch. 6, which presents this split as the baseline before Karnosky-Singer.
notes.regime_detection_hmm: despite the name, this is a STATIONARY 2-component Gaussian mixture fitted by EM, not a hidden Markov model: there is no transition matrix, so regime persistence/switching probability is not modelled, only the marginal mixture. A genuine HMM (Hamilton 1989, Econometrica 57(2)) fits a Markov-switching autoregression with an explicit 2x2 transition matrix. Flagged in engine/portfolio_factor.py so the function name isn't mistaken for a claim of Markov-switching behaviour; renaming it is a larger, separate change than the docstring fix.
notes.transaction_cost_analysis: quantity-weighted slippage vs an arrival/VWAP benchmark, in bps. A narrower measure than Perold's full implementation-shortfall decomposition: no delay cost or unexecuted- share opportunity-cost leg. No published source reproduces this exact quantity — checked, not assumed (Tier 3 #2 audit).
notes.rebalancing_optimiser: `no_trade_band` is a user-supplied absolute weight threshold, not one derived from cost/volatility parameters the way Leland (1999) or Donohue & Yip (2003) derive an optimal no-trade region. No published source reproduces this function's exact numbers — checked, not assumed (Tier 3 #2 audit).
notes.carbon_footprint_attribution: the WACI leg matches TCFD's definition exactly. The total_financed_emissions leg does NOT match either TCFD's or PCAF's financed-emissions standard: both use an ownership-share method, whereas this function uses revenue-intensity-times-invested-value. Flagged as a likely correctness question for the domain owner, not merely a citation gap (Tier 3 #2 audit).
